To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hydrolysis and reduction of the visual pigment photoproducts occur at different rates in cones and rods.
the hydrolysis reaction of the Schiff base linkage of the photolyzed visual pigment in cones occurs at least 2 orders of magnitude faster as compared to rods.
(1) The hydrolysis of 3-dehydro-retinal/opsin linkage is approximately 2-3 orders of magnitude faster in cones than in rods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of the late stages in the photolysis and regeneration of visual pigments, the processes which constitute the basis of dark adaptation.
the mechanisms of dark visual pigment regeneration in cones and in rods.
the mechanisms of the dark adaptation of cone and rod photoreceptor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fast hydrolysis reaction of the cone visual pigment is an adaptation to the diurnal lifestyle of the cone photoreceptors.
the fast photolysis of cone visual pigments in the dark is a key element of cone photoreceptors that is essential to their function in diurnal vision.
cones are more adapted to bright light than rods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photolysis and regeneration of the visual pigments in cones is faster than in rods, which is a prerequisite for the faster dark adaptation of cones as compared to rods.
the cone visual pigment is much more photolabile than the rod pigment, which is consistent with the fact that cones are much more light sensitive than rods.
the rate of the late stages in the photolysis reaction in cones is approximately 10-20 times faster than in rods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cones are more efficient in the utilization of light energy than rods.
the photolysis and regeneration of the visual pigment are faster and therefore less energy consuming in cone photoreceptors than in rods.

the rate-limiting steps in the dark adaptation of rods are the slow hydrolysis of 3-dehydro retinal from the opsin Schiff base (t1/2 approximately 100 s at 20 degrees) and the slow regeneration of retinol from 3-dehydroretonl (t1/ 2 approximately 1000s at 20 deg C).
